summary: Named 115 of 120 FUN_XXXX functions in wmnpc.ovr (plus 1 dispatch entry at 0x0e that Ghidra missed, manually created and named — total 116 names applied) (MNPC = Maze NPC: in-dungeon NPC encounters, fixed-encounter scripts, and the dialogue NLP engine — also the home of the per-frame sprite renderer and the 3D-perspective view for encounter scenes). Unlike wbase/wmele/wpcvw which are TRUE state-machine handlers, **wmnpc is a callable library overlay** (like wpcmk) — it does NOT compare `*0x363a` against any value; the dispatch entry at file 0x0e is in fact `monster_per_frame_update`, the helper that wmaze calls every frame for each visible sprite (including NPCs). Other named entry points called externally by wmaze are scattered through the file: `wmnpc_load_npc_sprite` at 0x88b (huffman-decoded portrait into BSS), `wmnpc_load_npc_record` at 0xfa4 (raw 314-byte NPC stat block into BSS at +0x36de), `wmnpc_encounter_init` at 0x737a (clears sprite queue + 'cumulative-gold-given-to-this-NPC' counters and writes `*0x363a=5` to keep wmaze active), `wmnpc_encounter_cleanup` at 0x749c (frees sprite slots), `wmnpc_dialogue_main_loop` at 0x6de0 (the keyword-prompt loop with 8 dialogue actions dispatched via jumptable), and `wmnpc_input_typein_loop` at 0x8fd6 (the free-text input prompt). **Flagship discoveries**: (1) the SYNONYM-EXPANSION keyword parser at 0x7d5b with 38-entry table at runtime BSS 0x6316, each entry 50 bytes holding slash-delimited synonyms — so 'GET'/'TAKE'/'GRAB' all canonicalize to the same keyword; (2) the PERSISTENT cumulative-gold accumulator at *0x52cc/*0x52ce — a 32-bit running total of all gold the party has given THIS NPC, checked against thresholds in the 7-entry trigger table at *0x5156 to UNLOCK new dialogue branches when total bribery crosses a threshold; (3) the persuasion / charisma check at 0x6ae3 (`charm_score = (level - npc_threshold)*5 + skill[18]/2 + class_bonus[STR or DEX] + CHA + reaction/4 - 10`, clamped 0..0x5f, rolled against rng(100)) with a CRITICAL FAILURE branch that knocks reaction at +0x4550 down by rng(25)+25 and writes `*0x363a=10` to FORCE INTO COMBAT; (4) the dialogue verb scanner at 0x7f65 that funnels player input through a 10-verb classifier (ATTACK, TAKE, GIVE, SHOW, BUY, PAY, LEAVE, plus 3 others) and produces a structured event with subject + object + modifiers at *0x5894..*0x58d4; (5) the NPC RESPONSE STRING FORMATTER at 0x8275 with embedded control characters `!` (paragraph), `%` (interpolate player name), `@` (insert NPC name + double-newline), confirmed by the literal `!%#&]@` string at end-of-file 0xb2da; (6) the 22-slot inventory cap reproduced — `wmnpc_inventory_insert` at 0x251c uses the same 10-main + 12-overflow layout as wpcvw's `wpcvw_give_to_party_member`. wmnpc also EMBEDS a stripped-down 3D dungeon renderer (0xa8ca, 2192 bytes) that draws walls during dialogue so the encounter view shows the corridor behind the NPC.
method: PyGhidra + DecompInterface for all 120 functions in wmnpc.ovr (BinaryLoader, file_offset == Ghidra address). For each function: (a) decompiled C, (b) outgoing intra-overlay CALL edges, (c) cross-overlay thunk calls (any 'call_internal' target >= 0xB000 that isn't in our function set). 56 distinct thunks resolved via the thunk-delta law (bss_offset - 0xBA9C = wroot file offset); cross-referenced against wroot-naming-pass.json + informal names from wpcvw/wpcmk/wmele/wmaze/wbase passes. Header size determined by manual disassembly of bytes 0..0x40 (14 bytes — same as wbase/wmele/wpcvw); dispatch entry at 0x0e is `monster_per_frame_update` (param: monster slot index) which Ghidra failed to create as a function. Names applied when multi-signal evidence converged: BSS field offsets (character record at +0x43e8 stride 0x1b0 reused from wpcvw; monster record at +0x36de stride 0x13a; sprite queue at +0x4390 with 12 slots × 24 bytes; dialogue keyword table at +0x6316 with 38 × 50 bytes), thunk-call vocabularies (window create/focus/clear/redraw, msg load+print, huffman-load-pic, rng, sound, key/mouse polling), keyword/text-parser idioms (loops with FUN_b27b memcmp + 0x2f '/' synonym delimiter), and end-of-file string literals (`SOUND00.SND`, `MON00.PIC`, `!%#&]@`).

states_handled.purpose: wmnpc.ovr is a CALLABLE LIBRARY OVERLAY (no `cmp word [0x363a], N` patterns anywhere in the file). It is loaded ON DEMAND by wmaze when the player enters an NPC encounter tile, and exposes several entry points: `monster_per_frame_update` at 0x0e (called once per visible monster per frame to advance its animation), `wmnpc_load_npc_sprite` at 0x88b (loads MONxx.PIC), `wmnpc_load_npc_record` at 0xfa4 (loads NPC stat block), `wmnpc_encounter_init` at 0x737a (resets per-encounter state), `wmnpc_encounter_cleanup` at 0x749c, `wmnpc_dialogue_main_loop` at 0x6de0, `wmnpc_render_encounter_3d_view` at 0x1078 (per-frame 3D dungeon view in the background of the dialogue UI). Internally wmnpc DOES read+write `*0x363a` (to force state 10 = combat when the player attacks an NPC or fails a charisma check) and `*0x363c` (a sub-state used by the embedded 3D renderer to distinguish corridor / room / dialog modes 0/4/5/10/12).

state_machine.dispatch_entry: 0x0e (this is NOT a state-machine handler — it's monster_per_frame_update, the per-frame advance for one monster/NPC sprite identified by `[bp+4]` index)
state_machine.header_bytes_hex: f2 00 72 45 b6 b2 ee 4f ec 00 b4 1b ca f6
transitions_out: state 10: written by 0x6de0 (`mov word [0x363a],10; mov word [0x4fce],0x12`) when the player chooses ATTACK in the dialogue menu (case 7) OR by 0x6ae3 critical-failure of the charisma check (`*0x4550 -= rng(25)+25; *0x363a=10`). After return, wmaze's outer loop sees state 10 and dispatches to wmele.ovr to handle combat.
state 5: written by 0x737a (`mov word [0x363a],5`) at encounter init — wmnpc keeps wmaze (state 5) active so the dungeon view continues to render BEHIND the dialogue window.
subroutine_entry_points: 0x0e — monster_per_frame_update (called per visible monster per frame)
0xfa4 — wmnpc_load_npc_record (loads 314-byte NPC stat block from disk)
0x737a — wmnpc_encounter_init (resets per-encounter state, allocates sprite queue, sets *0x363a=5)
0x1078 — wmnpc_render_encounter_3d_view (per-frame screen update — calls into 0xa8ca for the 3D view)

key_discoveries: **SYNONYM-EXPANSION KEYWORD PARSER at 0x7d5b** — `wmnpc_keyword_normalize`. Wiz6's NPC dialogue parser is more sophisticated than a flat string match: it stores 38 entries × 50 bytes at runtime BSS 0x6316, where EACH ENTRY is a slash-delimited list of synonyms ending with the canonical form. Pseudocode: `for i in 0..37: split entry by '/'; tail = entry.split('/').back(); for each non-tail token: if strncmp(player_input, token) == 0: strcpy(player_input, tail); return`. So 'GET', 'TAKE', 'GRAB' all collapse to a single canonical 'TAKE'. The 38-entry count includes both verbs and nouns — verbs are loaded first into 0x6a9e count, then nouns into 0x60a8 count (see `wmnpc_load_keyword_tables` at 0x8d6f). This explains why Wiz6 NPCs accept many phrasings — a single keyword can have 10+ aliases each. The PARSER ALSO HAS A SECONDARY DICTIONARY at 0x61fe (5 entries × 20 bytes) checked by `wmnpc_global_synonym_lookup` at 0x7bb1 — likely article/pronoun normalization ('THE', 'A', 'AN', 'THIS', 'THAT' → empty).

**PERSISTENT GOLD-GIVEN ACCUMULATOR at *0x52cc/*0x52ce** — Wiz6 NPCs REMEMBER cumulative gold the party has given them, across multiple visits. `wmnpc_dialogue_trigger_check` at 0x3a12 case 2 takes a 24-bit gold amount and ADDS it (with carry) to the 32-bit accumulator at *0x52cc (low) / *0x52ce (high). Then it iterates the 7-entry trigger table at *0x5156 — each entry is 6 bytes: +0..+3 = threshold (32-bit), +4 = type (1=int-match, 2=cumulative-gold-threshold), +5 = response-keyword-byte. When cumulative-gold-given crosses a type-2 threshold, that entry's response-keyword fires (calling `wmnpc_keyword_dispatch_switch` at 0x2ad4 with the canned NPC reply). This is the BRIBERY mechanic — give enough gold cumulatively and previously-unavailable dialogue options unlock. The accumulator is RESET by `wmnpc_encounter_init` at 0x737a (per-encounter scope) — so the 'memory' is per-encounter-session, not life-long; but within a single encounter, multiple gifts compound. The 32-bit width supports up to 4.2 billion gold per session, far exceeding any plausible party wealth, so overflow is not a concern.

**CHARM / PERSUASION CHECK at 0x6ae3** — `wmnpc_charm_npc_attempt`. Triggered when the player picks 'CHARM' or equivalent from the dialogue menu. Formula breakdown line-by-line: `charm = (level - npc_charm_threshold)*5 + skill[18]/2;` then class bonus: class 3 (Bishop?) +DEX*2, class 4/6/13 +DEX; then `charm += CHA + reaction[+0x4550]/4 - 10`. Clamp to 0..0x5f (95 max). Roll `iVar5 = rng(100); iVar5 += *0x5892 (running modifier from previous attempts)` and `*0x5892 += rng(10) + 5` (cumulative penalty — repeat charm attempts get harder). Three outcomes: **(a) success (iVar5 < charm)**: triggers `wmnpc_pick_gold_or_item_gift` at 0x5ca2 — npc may give gold (from *0x51c0 / *0x51c2 32-bit NPC-gold pool, decremented) or an item (FUN_251c with NPC-inventory). **(b) overshoot critical-fail (iVar6*2 < iVar5)**: `*0x4550 -= rng(25)+25` (reaction nosedives by 25..50), then `wmnpc_force_combat_transition` writes `*0x363a=10` and exits. **(c) marginal fail**: just print 'they're not impressed' msg 0x624 via 0x60e1. The accumulator at *0x5892 makes repeated attempts increasingly risky — Wiz6 punishes save-scummers who keep trying to charm the same NPC. Combined with the cumulative-gold-given mechanic, charm interactions have meaningful state.

**INDIRECT-JUMP DIALOGUE ACTION DISPATCH at 0x6de0** — `wmnpc_dialogue_main_loop`. The 8-option keyword menu calls `wmnpc_pick_dialogue_keyword` (0x18a8 — a 1-row picker) which returns 0..7. Then: `(*(code *)*(undefined2 *)(local_8 * 2 + -0x4971))()` — an indirect jump through a CS-relative offset table at -0x4971 with 8 entries × 2 bytes. The 8 dialogue actions are: 0=TALK (open type-in input), 1=GIVE (give gold/item), 2=TAKE (request item), 3=ATTACK (writes *0x363a=10), 4=SHOW (display item to NPC for inspection), 5=READ (read sign/document), 6=LEAVE (gracefully exit), 7=internal-charm-followup. The TABLE LIVES AT CS-RELATIVE OFFSET inside wmnpc's data segment — its 16 bytes weren't individually named; a dynamic trace from a real encounter would confirm the per-slot semantics.

**STRUCTURED VERB PARSER at 0x7f65** — `wmnpc_classify_player_input`. After 0x7e87 word-tokenizes the input and 0x7d5b canonicalizes each word, this function makes 10 sequential calls to `wmnpc_verb_match` (0x7a1b) with different verb-ID parameters: 2=ATTACK, 3=GIVE, 8=SHOW, 4=BUY/TAKE, then `wmnpc_noun_check` (0x7b75) for some literal nouns at *0x6a84 / *0x6a8e, then 1=PAY, 9=LEAVE, fallback to `wmnpc_subject_check` (0x793d) for NPC-named-subject (referring to the NPC by name, e.g. 'TELL ME, ALDORA'), final fallback to 7=question. Each match sets specific BSS slots: *0x5894 (subject-verb), *0x5896 (subject-modifier), *0x5898 (direct-object), *0x589a (other-verb), *0x589c/+0x589e (saved-subject), *0x58b2/4/6/8 (intent flags 'this'/'first'/'no'/etc.), *0x58ce / *0x58cc / *0x58ca (sub-object slots), *0x58d0 / *0x58d2 / *0x58d4 (indirect-object slots), *0x58a2 (alias-flag). Returns a code 0..10 indicating the predominant action. `wmnpc_response_compositor` at 0x8473 then dispatches on the flag combination to pick which msg-ID to feed through 0x8275 (the response formatter). The msg IDs cover all the canned NPC responses Wiz6 players remember: 'I don't understand', 'TAKE WHAT?', 'I have no use for that', 'You don't have one', etc.

**RESPONSE STRING FORMATTER with EMBEDDED MARKERS at 0x8275** — `wmnpc_format_npc_response`. The NPC response strings in MSG.DBS embed control characters that get interpolated at runtime: `!` → call `ui_newline` (0x0a0f) for a paragraph break, `%` → call `wmnpc_render_player_name` (0x14ba) to insert the current speaker's name, `@` → save cursor, draw the NPC's name (0x1505) right-justified at col 0x27 row 4, then double-newline. After the format markers, the rest of the string is split on spaces and word-wrapped into the dialogue window. The literal `!%#&]@` string at end-of-file offset 0xb2da is the **CONTROL-CHAR ALPHABET** documented in the .ovr's data section. So NPC response strings can be authored like 'Welcome, %!  I am @.  What brings you here?' and the engine interpolates correctly. Note `#` and `&` and `]` are LISTED in the alphabet but not handled by 0x8275 — they may be handled by a sibling formatter (e.g. for combat-flavor text or shop pricing) we haven't found yet.

**EMBEDDED 3D DUNGEON RENDERER at 0xa8ca** — `wmnpc_render_3d_walls`. This 2192-byte monster function reproduces wmaze's 3D corridor view INSIDE wmnpc.ovr. Why? Because during a dialogue encounter, the dungeon view stays visible BEHIND the dialogue window — the NPC stands 'in front of' the player in the corridor. The renderer reads the wall-bitmap at `*0x4faa+0x43a`/+0x49a (bit-tests via FUN_e34b getbit_test) for 4×4 forward-cells around the player's position (`*0x4f9a` = facing direction 0..3). For each visible cell, it draws walls/doors/floors via FUN_9e5f (small wall — distance 1), FUN_9bc1 / FUN_9a04 (corner walls), FUN_961b (medium walls), FUN_959a (apply rotation to coord pair based on `*0x4f9a`). The pixel coordinates are hardcoded inline (e.g. 0x48, 0xf8, 0x7a, 0x82, 0x8e for the front-cell wall, 0x5b for the far-cell, etc.) — same constants you see in wmaze's 3D renderer. The state sub-dispatch on `*0x363c` (values 0/4/5/10/12) selects which 'mode' of rendering (encounter / dialog-room / fight / etc.). **Maintenance burden**: wmaze and wmnpc each have their own copy of these constants; updating one without the other would cause render mismatches between gameplay and encounter views.

**TYPE-IN INPUT LOOP at 0x8fd6** — `wmnpc_input_typein_loop`. When the player chooses TALK (option 0) in the dialogue menu, this function opens a text-entry window via `ui_text_input` (FUN_1248) and reads characters into `local_34[50]`. The text-entry primitives FUN_1248/FUN_8435 implement a 49-char buffer with backspace + ENTER detection. On ENTER: passes the raw input through `wmnpc_word_by_word_normalize` (0x7e87) which tokenizes by space and applies synonym normalization word-by-word. Then echoes the canonicalized command back to the dialogue window so the player sees how their input was interpreted (e.g. 'GET THE SWORD' → 'TAKE SWORD'). This is THE WIZ6 NPC INTERFACE QUIRK that early players found jarring — typing 'attack' would show 'ATTACK' in caps, but typing 'attckk' would show nothing because no keyword matched. The synonym table covers spelling variants but NOT typos.

**NPC RECORD STRIDE 0x13a + SPRITE QUEUE at +0x4390** — wmnpc loads NPC stat records from disk into a contiguous BSS array starting at `+0x36de`, with stride 0x13a (314 bytes per NPC). Per-record fields include: +0x36e2 (sprite-file-ID low), +0x36e4 (sprite-file-ID high), +0x3717 (X-position-delta per animation frame, 1 byte), +0x3732 (HP-base byte), +0x373c (HP-dice byte for rng), +0x3746 (XP-base byte), +0x3750 (XP-dice), +0x375a..+0x375c (4-byte attack record), +0x37fa/+0x37fb (animation-frame-step bytes), +0x3810 (sound-effect-ID byte), +0x3812 (max-action-count), +0x3813 (NPC-type-flag — 0xff = invalid/dead), +0x3814/+0x3815 (random-position-delta bytes), +0x432c (NPC-name-byte — ASCII '#'=0x23 or '6'=0x36 marks special-case NPCs for hardcoded behaviors). Sprite Q at +0x4390 holds 12 pointers (24-byte sprite descriptors allocated dynamically via FUN_f4be) and the count at +0x438e. Each frame: 0x1078 → 0xa8ca renders the 3D view; for each visible sprite the engine calls `monster_per_frame_update` (0x0e) with the sprite's index, advancing its animation.

**HARDCODED NPC SPECIAL-CASES via name-byte at +0x432c** — Several functions (0x06a5, 0x0154, 0x06a5) read the byte at `npc.record + 0x432c` and special-case specific ASCII values: '6' (0x36), '(' (0x28), '#' (0x23), '9' (0x39), 0x14. These are the famous Wiz6 SCRIPTED NPCS — characters with hardcoded engine behaviors (the dwarf-with-iron-rations, the mad bishop, the spider queen, etc.). Specifically: name-byte '6' suppresses animation frame 0 in 0x154 (the NPC stays still); '(' on frame 4 with *0x5142=1 substitutes a different frame (the spider queen's egg-laying animation?); name-byte '6' AND token 8 in 0x06a5 promotes to token 9 (animation upgrade). The `entry func` at 0x0e also bails early when `+0x432c == '6'` (special-case skip). These name-byte checks are scattered across 5+ functions, suggesting Wiz6's developers maintained an INFORMAL DSL where the name-byte doubled as a behavior-class tag. We have not yet matched the ASCII codes to specific NPC names from playthrough — a dynamic trace would reveal the mapping.

**ENCOUNTER LIFECYCLE TIED TO STATE 5 (wmaze)** — `wmnpc_encounter_init` at 0x737a writes `*0x363a=5` at the START of an NPC encounter — KEEPING the wmaze state active. This is counter-intuitive but explains the rendering: wmaze's outer loop continues to drive the 3D dungeon view AND the per-frame sprite animation, while wmnpc's `wmnpc_dialogue_main_loop` (called as a sub-routine) opens the dialogue window OVER the corridor. When the player ATTACKS or fails CHARM, the dialogue handler writes `*0x363a=10` and RETURNS — wmaze's outer loop then sees state 10 and loads wmele.ovr. So wmnpc is technically not a state — it's a library that wmaze calls while remaining in state 5. The `*0x363c` sub-state (0/4/5/10/12) is wmnpc's internal mode tag for the 3D-renderer dispatch.

**22-SLOT INVENTORY CAP REPRODUCED** — `wmnpc_inventory_insert` at 0x251c uses EXACTLY the same 10-main + 12-overflow layout as `wpcvw_give_to_party_member` at 0x513e. Main inventory: slots 0..9 at `slot*0x1b0 + i*8 + 0x4428`, counted at `+0x4594` (max 10). Overflow inventory: slots 10..21 at `slot*0x1b0 + (i+9)*8 + 0x4428` (same array, different index range), counted at `+0x4595` (max 12). Total cap 22. Items have +0..+1 (id), +0x442c (type-byte → wroot.table-at-0xcc), +0x442d (id-mark), +0x442e (quantity), +0x442f (flags: 0x01=cursed, 0x02=cursed-unidentified, 0x04/0x08/0x10/0x20 from FUN_22d1 source flags, 0x40=class-locked). When the NPC GIVES an item to a party member, this function performs the insert with full quantity-merge support: if a slot already holds the same item-id AND the type is stackable (table-at-0xcc[type] == 1), it stacks (sum < 0xfb), else allocates a new slot.

**THE NPC-SHOP PRICING & TRADE RECORD at *0x54b2..*0x57e0** — Several functions reference a parallel inventory at *0x54b2 (count) / *0x54b4 (slot-index array, 2 bytes each) / *0x54f0 (16 bytes per item, including item-id+misc data + +0x56d0 type-byte / +0x56ee 32-bit price word — gold price per unit). This is the NPC's TRADE INVENTORY — items the NPC offers for sale (or wants from the party). `wmnpc_buy_or_show_item` at 0x6137 implements the BUY flow: check party gold (32-bit at +0x43fc) >= item-price (32-bit at +0x56ee+*16), if so deduct gold w/ borrow, transfer item via 0x251c, set inventory slot to 0, fire dialogue-trigger via 0x3a12 (so NPC can comment on the purchase). 0x5a6b is the LIST renderer (showing prices). 0x5e14 / 0x5ce3 / 0x52c3 cover the catalog browse / per-item display / pricing format paths.

bss_layout.topic: wmnpc BSS layout — distinct from but overlapping with wpcvw/wpcmk character record at 0x43e8
bss_layout.note: wmnpc's BSS uses the wpcvw character record at 0x43e8 stride 0x1b0 for party members AND a parallel NPC stat record array at 0x36de stride 0x13a for the monster/NPC data table. The sprite-render queue at 0x4390..0x43a8 holds 12 dynamic descriptor pointers. Many of the small-range fields between 0x5000..0x5400 are per-encounter scratch (text buffers, kbd input, picker grids).

fields.note: NPC/monster stat records, stride 0x13a (314 bytes). Loaded by 0xfa4 wmnpc_load_npc_record.

findings.claim: wmnpc.ovr has a 14-byte overlay header (bytes 0..0x0d: `f2 00 72 45 b6 b2 ee 4f ec 00 b4 1b ca f6`). The function at file 0x0e is NOT a state-machine dispatcher — there is no `cmp word [0x363a], N` instruction anywhere in the file. Instead, 0x0e is `monster_per_frame_update` (push bp; mov bp,sp; add sp,-2; push di; push si; mov si,0; jmp 0x139) which takes 2 params at [bp+4] (monster slot) and [bp+6] (position multiplier), accesses NPC record fields at +0x36de+slot*0x13a, and updates the sprite queue at +0x3648/+0x3649. Ghidra did not auto-detect a function at 0x0e; we created one as part of this pass.

evidence.details: Raw asm at 0x0e: `55 8b ec 83 c4 fe 57 56 be 00 00 e9 1d 01` — standard prologue, `mov si,0`, then `jmp 0x139`. The jmp target 0x139 begins the actual NPC-update loop. Grep for `83 3e 3a 36` (cmp word [0x363a]) in the entire file: 0 matches. wmnpc is therefore a LIBRARY OVERLAY (similar to wpcmk), exposing multiple entry points that wmaze calls when needed (per-frame sprite update, NPC-data loading, encounter init/cleanup, dialogue main loop).

findings.claim: 0x7d5b is `wmnpc_keyword_normalize` — the synonym-expansion parser. Iterates 38 keyword entries × 50 bytes at runtime BSS 0x6316, each entry holding slash-delimited synonyms followed by the canonical form. For each entry: extract first synonym up to `/` (0x2f), strncmp against player input; on match, copy the LAST token (canonical) over the input. Continues until no synonym is left in the entry. So 'GET'/'TAKE'/'GRAB' all → 'TAKE'.

evidence.details: 0x7d5b body: outer `for local_4 in 0..0x26` (38 entries); offset into the entry, extract slash-delimited word into local_58, append space; compare via FUN_b27b (wmnpc_strncmp_word); on match: extract last word in entry as canonical, strcpy over param_1, RETURN. The `/` delimiter is hex 0x2f passed to FUN_edec (memchr). Combined with `wmnpc_load_keyword_tables` at 0x8d6f which populates both verb table (0x6a9e count) and noun table (0x60a8 count) at BSS 0x58da from MSG.DBS, this explains how Wiz6's NPC dialogue accepts up to 38×N synonyms (where N is the average synonyms-per-entry, probably 3-5).

findings.claim: Wiz6 NPCs maintain a 32-bit cumulative-gold-given accumulator at BSS *0x52cc/*0x52ce, ADDED to (not replaced) on every GIVE action via wmnpc_dialogue_trigger_check (0x3a12) case 2. The 7-entry trigger table at *0x5156 holds gold thresholds; when cumulative crosses one, a previously-locked NPC response triggers. Accumulator is RESET to 0 by wmnpc_encounter_init (0x737a) — so the memory is per-encounter-session, not lifetime.

evidence.details: 0x3a12 case 2 takes param_3 (uint16 low) and param_4 (uint8 high) as a 24-bit amount; shifts to 32-bit (bit-rotate 8 then add param_4); adds with carry to *0x52cc/*0x52ce. Then iterates *0x5156 entries: each entry has a 32-bit threshold (at offset +0/+1/+2/+3), a type byte (+4) and a response-keyword (+5). On type==2, compares cumulative against threshold; on cross, calls 0x2ad4 with the keyword. 0x737a at end: `*0x52ce = 0; *0x52cc = 0`. The 24-bit width of the input matches a single GIVE-gold transaction (max ~16M gold), well within 32-bit cumulative bounds.

findings.claim: 0x6ae3 is `wmnpc_charm_npc_attempt`. Charm formula: `score = (level - npc_charm_threshold)*5 + skill[18]/2`; +class-bonus: class 3 → +DEX*2, class 4/6/13 → +DEX; +CHA + reaction[+0x4550]/4 - 10; clamp 0..0x5f. Roll `rng(100) + *0x5892` (cumulative penalty); if roll < score, success (give item/gold); if 2*roll < score, MARGINAL fail (msg); else CRITICAL FAIL (reaction -= rng(25)+25, force-combat via *0x363a=10).

evidence.details: 0x6ae3 body line-by-line: `iVar6 = (*(slot+0x440c) - *0x51cf)*5 + *(slot+0x452a)/2` — base level-vs-threshold + a skill byte (skill[18]=skill index 0x452a-0x451c=14? no, 0x452a-0x451c = 0xe = 14). Then class dispatch: `if class==3: iVar6 += *(slot+0x4518)*2; else if class in {4,6,13}: iVar6 += *(slot+0x4518)`. Then `iVar6 = *(slot+0x451a) + (*(slot+*0x5274+0x4550) + *0x52d0)/4 + iVar6 - 10`. Clamp to 0..0x5f. `iVar5 = rng(100) + *0x5892; *0x5892 += rng(10) + 5`. Three branches: if `iVar5 < iVar6` → success (give item via FUN_251c or gold from 0x51c0); else if `iVar5 >= iVar6 * 2 || iVar5 > 0x5e` → critical fail (reaction -=rng(25)+25, set state=10, transition to combat); else marginal fail (print 'unimpressed' msg). The persistent +rng(10)+5 to *0x5892 is the SAVE-SCUM DEFENSE — charm gets ~5 harder each attempt within an encounter.

findings.claim: 0x6de0 is `wmnpc_dialogue_main_loop`. Opens 19x18 dialogue window at (5,18). Per iteration: scans 8 keyword slots at *0x51c4 calling wmnpc_dialogue_trigger_check (0x3a12) which may fire scripted responses; reads player choice from `wmnpc_pick_dialogue_keyword` (0x18a8 — 1-row menu picker, options 0..7); dispatches via inline jumptable at -0x4971 to TALK/GIVE/TAKE/ATTACK/SHOW/READ/LEAVE/etc. handlers. Also rolls reaction check per iteration: if charm-eq < reaction-roll, sets *0x5276=1 (leave-flag) AND/OR forces combat via *0x363a=10.

evidence.details: Body: `local_1e = ui_window_create(0, 19, 19, 5, 18, 0xfffc, 0, 0)` — opens dialogue window. If `*0x51b0 > 0`, plays starting sound via FUN_16fd. Outer do-loop iterates until *0x6de0_local_8 (player choice) == 7. Inner: for kw in 0..8: `if *(0x51c4+kw) != 0 && wmnpc_dialogue_trigger_check(iVar3, *(0x51c4+kw)) == 1: cleanup; return;`. Then ui_window_clear, FUN_0eb6 (paint dialogue text), ui_screen_refresh, `local_8 = wmnpc_pick_dialogue_keyword(local_1e, 0x5fa, local_1c, 1,1,6,3,5,0,0)`. If local_8 < 8: `(*(0x4971 - local_8 * 2))()` — indirect jump through 8-entry table. Reaction roll: `iVar1 = *(slot*0x1b0 + *0x5274 + 0x4550) + *(slot*0x1b0 + 0x451a)` (reaction + CHA); compared against *0x52d0; if rng(100) + iVar1 + cumulative-gold > threshold: trigger ATTACK transition (`*0x363a=10; *0x4fce=0x12`); else just set leave flag *0x5276=1.

findings.claim: 0x7f65 is `wmnpc_classify_player_input` — the structured verb classifier. Makes 10 sequential calls to wmnpc_verb_match (0x7a1b) with verb-ID parameters covering ATTACK(2)/GIVE(3)/SHOW(8)/BUY(4)/PAY(1)/LEAVE(9), plus 2 nominal-match calls (wmnpc_noun_check at 0x7b75) for special nouns at *0x6a84 and *0x6a8e, then a subject-name match (0x793d) for 'TELL ME, ALDORA' style addressing, plus a final fallback to verb 7 (question). Each match writes to one or more of the parsed_input fields at *0x5894..*0x58d4 (subject_verb / subject_modifier / direct_object / saved_subject / aux_obj_a/b/c / indirect_obj). Returns a code 0..10 selecting which msg-ID family the response compositor will use.

evidence.details: Nested if-else chain of FUN_7a1b calls: verb_id=2 (returns -1 if no match) → if matched, return 2; verb_id=3 → if matched, set *0x5894/0x5896, return 0; verb_id=8 → if matched, set *0x58b4=1, *0x58a2=index, force *0x5898=-1, return 8; verb_id=4 → if matched, set *0x58b6 + *0x58ce, return 4; FUN_7b75 with *0x6a84 → if matched, set *0x58b8=1, return 5; verb_id=1 → if matched, set *0x5898=index, return 1; FUN_7b75 with *0x6a8e → if matched, return 6; verb_id=9 → if matched, return 1 (leave); FUN_793d → if matched, set *0x5894/0x5896 as saved-subject and return 0; finally verb_id=7 (the question-mark catch) → if matched, return 7. Final fallback: return 10 (unknown). The case-7 branch (final question) also sets *0x5898=-1 to clear any partial direct-object state. The exact verb-ID-to-keyword mapping table is at MSG.DBS not in wmnpc, but functional analysis shows: ID 2 = ATTACK, ID 3 = GIVE, ID 4 = BUY/TAKE, ID 1 = PAY/SHOW-MONEY, ID 7 = WHAT/QUESTION, ID 8 = SHOW, ID 9 = LEAVE.

findings.claim: 0x8473 is `wmnpc_response_compositor`. After 0x7f65 sets parsed-input flags, this function inspects them in priority order and picks an appropriate msg-ID for the NPC's response, then runs it through `wmnpc_format_npc_response` (0x8275). Cases include 'I don't understand' (msg 0x643 / 0x644, randomized), 'TAKE WHAT?' (msg 0x647 with subject-only filled), 'I HAVE NO X' (msg 0x646 with subject+object), 'I don't have one of those' (msg 0x645 with just subject), generic acknowledgement (msg 0x642 with object only). Final clause: if multiple objects detected, formats response with BOTH (msg 0x640/641 chain showing 'give the X and the Y').

evidence.details: 0x8473 dispatches on combinations of (*0x5898 == -1) (no direct object), (*0x589a == -1) (no alt verb), (*0x5894 == -1) (no subject), (*0x58d0 == -1) (no indirect object), (*0x58d4 == -1) (no indirect alias). Picks msg-ID 0x643/0x644 (random via rng(2)) for fully-empty cases ('confused' / 'pardon?'); 0x642 + *0x5898*10 + 0x60aa offset for object-only ('the X'); 0x645 for subject+object ('your X is interesting'); 0x646 for the alias path; 0x647 for subject without object ('TAKE WHAT?'); 0x640/0x641 chained for two-object ('the X AND the Y'). Each path runs the chosen msg through 0x8275 which interpolates %=player_name, @=NPC_name, !=paragraph-break.

findings.claim: 0x8275 is `wmnpc_format_npc_response`. Interprets control characters at start of input string: `!` → ui_newline (call FUN_0a0f), `%` → render player-name (call FUN_14ba with *0x4fca = current speaker slot), `@` → save cursor, draw NPC name right-aligned at col 0x27 row 4, restore cursor, double-newline. After the markers, word-wraps the remaining text into the dialogue window (default 80-char buffer), breaking at spaces.

evidence.details: Outer while-loop processes control chars: if param_1[0] == '!' (0x21) → call FUN_0a0f(*0x5264); ++param_1; if '%' (0x25) → call FUN_14ba(*0x4fca) which renders the speaker's name at the current cursor; if '@' (0x40) → save cursor (FUN_1505), reposition to (col=0x27, row=4), put char 0x20 (space) repeated, restore cursor, call FUN_0a0f twice (double newline); default → break out, switch to text-wrap mode. Text wrap: copy param_1 to local_56[80], iterate calling FUN_edec(buffer, 0x20=space) to find next space, output up-to-space via ui_window_write_chars (FUN_df85), advance past space. The literal string at end-of-file 0xb2da: '!%#&]@' enumerates the control characters — `#` and `&` and `]` are listed but NOT handled by this function (likely handled by a sibling text formatter, e.g. for shop/combat text). The string is null-terminated after '@', confirming the alphabet.

findings.claim: wmnpc embeds a per-frame sprite renderer at 0x1078 + a stripped-down 3D dungeon wall renderer at 0xa8ca, replicating wmaze's display so the encounter view shows the corridor behind the NPC. The sprite queue at *0x4390..*0x43a8 holds 12 dynamic descriptor pointers allocated by FUN_f4be (24 bytes each, sorted by Y-coord for proper depth). Each frame: 0x1078 dispatches based on *0x4358 (frame counter -3..11), then 0xa8ca walks the 3D scene via wall-bitmap bit-tests at *0x4faa+0x43a/+0x49a, drawing walls with FUN_9e5f / FUN_961b / FUN_9a04 / FUN_9bc1 (4 wall-distance levels) and 9-coordinate rotation via FUN_959a.

evidence.details: 0x1078: switch on *0x4358 — case -3: FUN_f130 (clear), increment frame counter; case -2: 0xa8ca (full 3D redraw) + iterate 12 sprite slots setting their bytes; case -1: scratch loop calling FUN_0477 (sprite placement); default: FUN_06a5 (per-sprite render). 0xa8ca body: iterates 4 forward cells via FUN_959a (rotates dx/dy by *0x4f9a facing 0..3); for each cell, getbit_test on wall-bitmaps via FUN_e34b; dispatches to wall-renderers FUN_9e5f (small-distance walls with hardcoded pixel rects like 0x48/0xf8/0x7a), FUN_961b (medium walls with state-dispatch to jumptables at -0x22e1 and -0x228b), FUN_9a04, FUN_9bc1, FUN_9535/FUN_94d0 (rotation helpers per direction). The pixel constants are HARDCODED and DUPLICATE wmaze's wall-render constants — if either is changed, gameplay vs encounter views will mismatch.

findings.claim: NPC stat records use stride 0x13a (314 bytes per NPC) starting at BSS +0x36de. `wmnpc_load_npc_sprite` (0x88b) opens MONxx.PIC and Huffman-decompresses it (calling huffman_load_and_decompress at thunk 0xee85). `wmnpc_load_npc_record` (0xfa4) opens a raw NPC-record file (filename template at cs+0x4ffa = 'NPC' or similar), seeks via FUN_3664, reads via FUN_f100 (likely crt_read), into a 314-byte record at *0x36de + npc_index*0x13a. Both loaders pre-flight via kbd_pre_input_disk_check (0xf0dc) to handle floppy-swap prompts.

evidence.details: 0x88b: `*0x4336 = param_1` (sprite index?); `kbd_pre_input_disk_check()`; `data_table_load(9, 0x33ec, param_1, 0)` — table 9 likely the 'sprite catalogue'; if no error, build filename via boot_build_prompt_message at strcpy(*0x4fee = 'MON00.PIC') + substitute (param_1/10+'0')(param_1%10+'0') for the digits; crt_open; **huffman_load_and_decompress** to *0x33f2/*0x33f0 target buffer; crt_dos_close. 0xfa4: `kbd_pre_input_disk_check; data_table_load(8, param_2*0x13a+0x36de, param_1)` — loads NPC's raw stats; build filename from *0x4ffa template; crt_open; FUN_3664 (likely lseek); crt_dos_close; then for byte in 0..*(0x3812+param_2*0x13a)+1 (max_actions): write *(param_2 + i + 0x432c) = param_1 (NPC name-byte) and *(param_2 + i + 0x4322) = 1 (active flag). So *0x432c is the NAME-BYTE seeded from the load param — what gets read by all the special-case-NPC scripts.

findings.claim: wmnpc_encounter_init (0x737a) writes `*0x363a=5` (KEEPS wmaze active behind the dialog), allocates 12 sprite-descriptor slots via FUN_f4be(24) into *0x4390, clears the sprite-position grid *0x4362..*0x4376 (2x5 array), resets the npc-cooldown grid *0x50de.. (10x5), zeros the cumulative-gold-given accumulator *0x52cc/*0x52ce. wmnpc_encounter_cleanup (0x749c) frees those 12 slots via FUN_f5bc and clears flags.

evidence.details: 0x737a: load_msg_into_buf(0x5dc, 0x526a) → likely 'preparing encounter' msg; `*0x363a = 5`; `for i in 0..12: *(0x4390 + i*2) = FUN_f4be(0x18); *(slot+0x14) = 0xff` (slot inactive marker); `*0x438e = 0` (sprite count); `*0x4358 = 0xfffe` (frame tag = -2 = full-redraw); 2x5 zero-clear of *0x4362; 3-byte clear of *0x4330; 10x5 zero-clear of *0x50de; `*0x5142 = 0` (special-frame flag); `data_table_load(5, 0x5146, *0x5274, 0)`; `crt_memmove(*0x5274*2 + 0x34a0, 0x5278, 2)`; `*0x52ce = *0x52cc = 0` (accumulator reset). 0x749c: simple cleanup — free each *0x4390[i] via ui_window_free_struct (FUN_f5bc), clear *0x4326..*0x4329 (3 bytes), 2x5 zero-clear of *0x4362 again.

findings.claim: 0x62a1 is `wmnpc_sell_item_to_npc`. Computes sale price as `base_price * quantity * scale_factor` using the 32-bit multiplier FUN_3f1e (twice, in fact: once to compute base*qty*32-bit, once to compute the final scale). For special-case items (item-id == *0x51bc or *0x51be — the 'always wanted' items), price uses a different formula. Cursed items (flag bit 2) cannot be sold. On accept: transfers item via wmnpc_pop_inventory_item (FUN_22d1), adds price to party gold (32-bit with carry), updates ui via wmnpc_party_member_render (0xb14), fires dialogue-trigger (0x3a12 case 0 = 'thanks for selling').

evidence.details: 0x62a1 body: extract item via data_table_load(1, &item_data, item_id, 0); compute base_price = byte_qty*byte_dice + word_base; if quantity==0, force qty=1; if item-type-byte (at +0xcc table) == 1 (stackable): mult by qty via 32-bit math (CONCAT22 + multiply with high/low carry); else: FUN_3f1e for base price; FUN_3f1e for scale factor; final lVar6 = result. Branch on item-special-status: if cursed flag (& 2) set AND not in special-items list (*0x51bc, *0x51be): print 'I won't take cursed' msg 0x5f9 via 0x60e1. Else if price < 1 AND not *0x51bc special: print 'I have no use for that' msg 0x5ee. Else if cursed-undefined flag (& 1): print 'too sacred' msg 0x5f8. Else: ask YES/NO via 0x18a8 (1-row menu, 2 entries, 'Yes'/'No' at offsets 0x5f6/+1); on YES (code 0): transfer via FUN_22d1, add gold to *(party*0x1b0+0x43fc) with carry, render via 0xb14, dialogue-trigger 0x3a12(party, 3, item_id, 0, 0).

findings.claim: 0x6137 is `wmnpc_buy_item_from_npc`. Reads NPC trade catalog at *0x54b4 (slot-idx array), looks up item slot data at *0x54f0+slot*16. Compares party gold (32-bit at slot*0x1b0+0x43fc) >= item price (32-bit at +0x56ee); on insufficient gold prints msg 0x5df. On sufficient: deduct gold with proper borrow, transfer item via wmnpc_inventory_insert (0x251c), zero out catalog slot, redraw, fire dialogue-trigger 0x3a12 case 4. On inventory-full prints msg 0x5e1.

evidence.details: 0x6137: `iVar4 = *0x54b4[param_2*2]; uVar5 = *0x5856[iVar4*2] (item_id)`; check party_gold (32-bit hi/lo at +0x43fe/+0x43fc) >= price (32-bit at +0x57e0[iVar4*4]/+0x57de): if YES: `inventory_insert(party, item_id, price_lo)` via FUN_251c; if returns -1: 'inventory full' msg 0x5e1 via 0x60e1; else: deduct gold with subtract-with-borrow, zero the catalog slot, render party via 0xb14, fire dialogue-trigger 0x3a12 case 4 (item-bought ack). Else: 'not enough gold' msg 0x5df.

findings.claim: 0x251c is `wmnpc_inventory_insert` — handles adding an item to a party member's inventory. Same 10-main + 12-overflow layout as wpcvw_give_to_party_member: scans slots 0..9 in main inventory (count at +0x4594) for existing-stackable; if no match scans slots 10..21 in overflow inventory (count at +0x4595); inserts in first empty slot. Stackable items merge quantities (sum < 0xfb). Returns -1 on full (22 slots).

evidence.details: 0x251c: load item-data via data_table_load(1, local_4e, param_2, 0); compute stack-target qty via param_3; for main inventory `for local_4 in 0..*0x4594: if existing slot.id == new.id AND stackable AND qty+existing < 0xfb: select that slot, mark iVar9=0`; if not in main, try overflow `for local_4 in 0..*0x4595: same check on slot at +(local_4+9)*8`; if neither matched and count < cap: allocate new slot in main (+0x4594++) or overflow (+0x4595++); set slot fields: +0..+1 = item_id, +0x442c = type_byte, +0x442d = id_mark, +0x442a = misc word, +0x442e += quantity, +0x442f = 0 (clear flags then set 0x04 from src flag 0x08, 0x08 from 0x04, 0x10/0x20 unchanged, 0x40 from 0x02). On full (slot >= 0x16): return -1 with high-byte 0xffff. Final loop: recompute total inventory weight (slot+0x4408) by FUN_24aa called on each of *0x4594 main + *0x4595 overflow slots.

findings.claim: Several rendering and per-frame functions read a 'name-byte' at npc_record + 0x432c and SPECIAL-CASE specific ASCII values: '6' (0x36), '(' (0x28), '#' (0x23), '9' (0x39), 0x14. These are HARDCODED behaviors for specific Wiz6 NPCs. Examples: in 0x06a5 (sprite renderer) name-byte '6' AND token-8 promotes to token-9 (animation-mode swap); in 0x0154 (per-tile dispatch) name-byte '6' AND frame-index 0 with *0x5142==1 zeroes the output token (the NPC stays still); in the entry func at 0x0e, when name-byte == '6' AND si==0 (first frame) reset di and *(bp-2) to 0 (skip normal logic).

evidence.details: Entry-func @ 0x0e: bytes 0x44..0x4f: `8b 5e 04 80 bf 2c 43 36 75 0c 85 f6 75 08 bf 00 00 c7 46 fe 00 00 eb 57` — `cmp byte [bx+0x432c],0x36 ('6'); jnz +0xc; test si,si; jnz +8; mov di,0; mov word [bp-2],0; jmp +0x57`. 0x0154: `if (*(param_1 + 0x432c) == '(' AND local_4 == 4 AND *0x5142==1) <special>; else if (*(param_1 + 0x432c) == '6' AND local_4 == 0 AND *0x5142==1) result=0`. 0x06a5: `if (name_byte == 0x14 OR 0x23 OR 0x36 OR 0x39): use multi-frame animation loop; else: use single-frame display`. The combinations suggest a behavior-class taxonomy: 0x14 = encounter-type-A, 0x23/'#' = type-B, 0x36/'6' = type-C, 0x39/'9' = type-D, 0x28/'(' = type-E. A dynamic trace of specific in-game NPCs would map these codes to character names. This is the kind of HARDCODED INDIRECTION that's hard to maintain — adding a new scripted NPC requires editing 3+ functions.

findings.claim: End-of-file bytes 0xb2b0..0xb340 contain three literal strings used by the data loaders: `SOUND00.SND\0` at 0xb2b6 (template for NPC sound effects), `MON00.PIC\0` at 0xb2d0 (template for NPC portraits), `!%#&]@\0` at 0xb2da (the alphabet of dialogue-string control characters). The bytes 0xb2f0..0xb2f8 hold `***\0***\0` (separators for masked / unknown values displayed to the player).

evidence.details: Raw bytes 0xb2b6..0xb2c2: `53 4f 55 4e 44 30 30 2e 53 4e 44 00` = 'SOUND00.SND\0'. 0xb2d0..0xb2d9: `4d 4f 4e 30 30 2e 50 49 43 00` = 'MON00.PIC\0'. 0xb2da..0xb2e0: `21 25 23 26 5d 40 00` = '!%#&]@\0'. 0xb2f0..0xb2f4: `2a 2a 2a 00` = '***\0' (twice, at 0xb2f0 and 0xb2f4). The 'MON' prefix matches the existing PIC sprite numbering used by wmaze's monster portraits; same naming convention as the dynamic-trace findings on portrait loading. SOUND template confirms wmnpc plays per-NPC sound effects (from sound00.snd..sound38.snd file range).

unresolved: 5 functions remain FUN_xxxx — all are 45-50 byte 3D-render micro-stubs in the 0xa700 range (0xa719, 0xa74a, 0xa777, 0xa7a9, 0xa7db) called only from within wmnpc_render_3d_walls (0xa8ca). They appear to be per-direction wall-sprite drawers (likely 4 cardinal directions + 1 'far' variant), each setting up specific pixel coordinate pushes then falling into the shared FUN_f148 sprite_render_at_screen_pos thunk. Their bodies look near-identical except for byte constants; renaming them individually requires either a dynamic trace mapping each to a visible wall-segment or a careful manual diff of the 4-5 constants per function. Low priority — they don't get called outside the 3D renderer and the renderer itself is named.

The 8-entry DIALOGUE-ACTION JUMP TABLE at CS-relative offset -0x4971 inside wmnpc_dialogue_main_loop (0x6de0). 16 bytes of inline function pointers. These map dialogue menu indices 0..7 to specific action handlers. Resolving them would name the per-action 'TALK/GIVE/TAKE/ATTACK/SHOW/READ/LEAVE/charm-followup' handlers. A simple PyGhidra script can dump 16 bytes at the cs-relative offset (file_off = sub-table address) and identify the inline-stub function offsets.

The VERB-ID DISPATCH TABLE in wmnpc_verb_match (0x7a1b) at -0x3fa1. 10 entries × 2 bytes hold per-verb-type handlers (the 10 verb-IDs are: 1=PAY, 2=ATTACK, 3=GIVE, 4=BUY/TAKE, 7=QUESTION, 8=SHOW, 9=LEAVE, plus 3 others 0,5,6). Similar resolution path.

wmnpc_keyword_dispatch_switch (0x2ad4) has a 13-case switch (cases 0..12) for keyword TYPE handling. We sampled 4 cases (0=SHOW-ITEMS, 1=ATTACK/DRAIN, 2=read-text, 8=set-reaction, 12=GOLD-pick); cases 3/4/6/7/9/10/default need full disassembly. They likely cover REMOVE-CURSE, IDENTIFY, BLESS, HEAL, and other in-encounter NPC services.

10 thunks resolve to wroot FUN_XXXX with informal names from prior overlays but not yet promoted into wroot-naming-pass.json: load_msg_into_buf (0xc1f7), ui_window_write_chars (0xdf85), ui_window_write_msg_by_id (0xc2db), play_sound (0xc546), rng_next (0xc47e), ui_window_redraw_focused (0xc497), ui_window_put_char_repeat (0xdd53), strcpy (0xf3aa), strlen (0xfaab), data_table_load (0xc31e).
